title: Behold, Amid His Little Flock
description: Behold, Amid His Little Flock in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Dale wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 683 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christ Blessing the Bread”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold, a-mid his lit-tle flock, The Sa-viour stands se-rene, Un-awed by suf-fering yet to be, Un-changed by what hath been.

lines: Unawed by suffering yet to be,
Still beams the light of love undimmed
Nor, save his own prophetic word,
Aught speaks him soon to die.
He pours within the votive cup
The rich blood of the vine,
And "Drink ye all the hallowed draught,"
He breaks the bread; then clasps his hands,
And lifts his eyes in prayer,
Receive ye this and view by faith

licence: Public domain: Thomas Dale died in 1870.
credits: Words by Thomas Dale (1797–1870), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
